title: The parent-child line in the destiny matrix: the childhood home you carry with you

seo.title: Parent-child karma in the destiny matrix: the A–O–J line
seo.description: Parent-child karma in the destiny matrix: three points on the left-hand spoke for parents, attitude to children and outer expression. Calculate and read yours.
queries: parent-child karma in the destiny matrix
parent-child line in the destiny matrix

meaning: The parent-child line — also called parent-child karma, the parent-child channel, or DRK for short, after its Russian initials — is a set of three points on the left-hand spoke of the destiny matrix. J stands for your parents and the atmosphere you grew up in. O is your attitude to children. A is your outer expression: how the world sees you.

The line is read starting from the parents: from the home of your childhood, to how you behave around younger people, and on out into the world. It is calculated from your date of birth alone: J = A + centre, O = A + J, and any sum above 22 is reduced by adding its digits. There are 255 possible triples. You do not need a parent's or a child's date for this line, and everyone has one, including adults without children.

paragraphs: The triple is written in this order, A–O–J, but read from the bottom up: from the childhood home at J to the outer expression at A.

"Karma" and "channel" are simply everyday names for the same line. Lines in the matrix are often called channels — the money channel, the relationship channel — and the parent-child channel is this same A–O–J triple. "Karma" in the name does not mean a debt or a punishment: it means a familiar family pattern that keeps repeating until someone notices it.

Your own triple appears in the ordinary free calculation: the numbers are on the diagram and in the "Parent-child line" section. What each arcanum means in each of the three roles is collected in the table below.

article_sections.h2: Where to find the parent-child line in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: The matrix is drawn as an eight-pointed star. The upright square has four corners: the day of birth A on the left, the month B at the top, the year C on the right and the karmic task D at the bottom, with the centre E in the middle. The parent-child line is the **left-hand spoke**, running from the day corner to the centre. The outer point is the corner A itself. The point nearest the centre is J. O sits between them.

Going from the edge to the centre, the order is A — O — J — E. The triple is written the same way, **A–O–J**, but read in reverse, starting from J. This is how Yuliana Lisovskaya reads the line: first the atmosphere a person grew up in, then what they carried from it into their attitude to children, and finally how all of this comes out into the world. The centre E is used in the calculation, but it does not become a fourth role in the line.

paragraphs: On the site's diagram the points carry only letters, numbers and labels — no symbols. In the full reading the line gets a section of its own, "Parent-child line". It follows straight after "Relationships" and before "Karma of relationships with parents and children": from your partner, to your own line with parents and children, and then on to the family patterns of your lineage.

If you have opened the chakra table, you have already seen these three numbers. **A, O and J sit in the physics column:** A at Sahasrara, O at Ajna, J at Vishuddha. Across all 46,334 dates since 1900 the match is exact. But these cells have their own meaning in the chakra table, and there is no need to rewrite the Ajna reading "about children": one point simply takes part in two readings.

article_sections.h2: How to calculate parent-child karma from your date of birth
paragraphs: Every sum is reduced the same way: **a number above 22 is replaced by the sum of its digits.** 29 → 2 + 9 = 11, 32 → 3 + 2 = 5, while 22 stays as the twenty-second arcanum, The Fool. Here is the line for 12 April 2016 — five additions in all.

ol: **Portrait, month and year.** A is the day of birth, 12 (a day above 22 is reduced too: 25 → 7, 31 → 4). B is the month, 4. C is the sum of the year's digits: 2 + 0 + 1 + 6 = 9.
**Centre of the matrix** E = A + B + C + D = 12 + 4 + 9 + 7 = 32 → 5.

paragraphs: That gives the line **12-11-17**: The Hanged Man, Strength, The Star.

A second date shows what to do with 22. For 5 September 1990: A = 5, B = 9, C = 1 + 9 + 9 + 0 = 19, D = 5 + 9 + 19 = 33 → 6, E = 5 + 9 + 19 + 6 = 39 → 12. Then J = 5 + 12 = 17, and O = 5 + 17 = 22. Twenty-two is not reduced: The Fool stands in the attitude to children. The line is **5-22-17**.

paragraphs.h3: How to check yourself: add the ends

paragraphs: The middle of the line always equals the reduced sum of the two outer numbers: 12 + 17 = 29 → 11. If yours doesn't add up, look for a mistake in the centre or in a reduction. D is the usual culprit: a wrong bottom corner pulls the centre off with it, and J and O along with it.

The numbers themselves can give a mistake away. **O and J are never 1 or 2:** both points are sums in which one of the numbers is at least 3. And A always equals the day of birth reduced to 22 or less: 3 for people born on the 30th, 4 for those born on the 31st.

paragraphs: **It shares no points with the "Parents and children" section.** For 12.04.2016 that section reads 16-13-16 — The Tower, Death, The Tower — while the line reads 12-11-17. Checking every date since 1900 turned up none where the two triples match. The F/G/H section asks which rules came down the male and female branches of your family and what you pass on. The A–O–J line asks what home you absorbed personally and how it sounds in you now. The questions are neighbours but not the same, which is why the report has two sections side by side.

**Compatibility is a different calculation.** If your question is "how do I get on with my child?", you need a matrix of two people: the points of two personal charts are added together to make a third chart, which can even contain numbers that never appear in a personal one. Your own A–O–J line cannot answer that question: it describes you, not you and your child together. And the couple's matrix has its own area called "The couple as parents" — that is about two partners raising a child together, not about a parent's relationship with a son or daughter.

article_sections.h2: Three roles: parents, attitude to children, outer expression

paragraphs.h3: J — parents and the atmosphere of childhood

paragraphs: Lisovskaya calls this the parents' point. It describes the atmosphere a person was born and raised in, the upbringing and the mood around them as a child, and how the relationship between the adults at home left its mark. The point can be read even if the parents are no longer alive or were never around: it is about the atmosphere a person absorbed, not about the biography of particular people.

For Lisovskaya, the children's point reaches beyond your own children. It is your attitude to children in general: wanting or not wanting them, your fears, how you behave around a child — your own, a younger brother, a pupil, the neighbours' toddler. In her words, O "always interacts" with the parents' point: what you absorbed, you carry forward — either repeating the pattern or doing the exact opposite. For someone without children this is the role of the elder; for a child, it is how they treat those younger than themselves. The point says nothing about future offspring.

The birth-day corner, labelled the personality portrait on the diagram. In this line it plays a special role: it is the "mask" through which a person looks at the world and takes it in. Lisovskaya writes that the family has a strong influence on exactly this point: our sense of reality and our way of showing up in it come from the family. That is why the line ends here — family experience comes out through your familiar image.
Take Strength, the eleventh arcanum, and place it at each point in reading order, starting from the parents.

ul: **At J**, Strength is a home of strong characters. Endurance was valued, difficulties were overcome, complaining was not the done thing, and pressure sometimes took the place of conversation.
**At O**, it is your attitude to younger people. To protect, toughen up, teach them not to give in; on its negative side, to push and demand resilience when a child needs a break.
**At A**, it is how people see you: a strong, resilient person others turn to for support.

paragraphs: One card, three different questions: what was around you, what you do with younger people, and what others see. That is why an arcanum's meaning in this line is always read together with its point.

paragraphs: Three things this table makes visible:

ul: **The Magician and The High Priestess never appear at O or J.** Both points are sums of two numbers, one of them at least 1 and the other at least 3. Sums up to 22 stay as they are, and sums from 23 to 44 never reduce to less than 3 (30 → 3). In outer expression, 1 and 2 occur for people born on the 1st and 2nd of the month.
**At A, the numbers 3–11 are the most common** — each for 5–7% of dates. Days 23 to 31 reduce to these numbers, so each of them gets two days a month, while 12–22 get one.
**At O, 5–11 come up most often**, while at J the numbers are spread more evenly. The rarest at J are The Empress and The Emperor, at about 2% of dates each.

paragraphs: Where the keys come from: Lisovskaya describes the roles of the three points, and the wording for each role is our adaptation of her descriptions of the twenty-two energies. In the book the energies are described in general terms, not broken down by the points of the line.

article_sections.h2: How to join three arcana into one idea
paragraphs: A list like "The Star — a home of hopes, Strength — protection, The Hanged Man — waiting" doesn't explain anything yet: it doesn't show how these three things live together in one person. The meaning appears when the cards answer a shared question — what you took from home and how it lives in you now.

ol: **Start with J.** It sets the theme of the whole line: what the air was like at home. Read the other points as an answer to it.
**See what O does with that atmosphere.** Does it repeat it — so that around younger people you hear the tones of your own childhood? Or does it turn it upside down — "it won't be like that with me"?
**Find how A carries it outwards.** How people see you, and the "mask" through which you look at the world.
**Put it into one idea** that needs all three cards. If the idea still holds after you swap one card for another, it is too general.

paragraphs: Order matters. 5-22-17 and 17-22-5 are made of the same numbers, but they are different lines. In the first, The Star is the home and The Hierophant is the outer expression. In the second, the home is The Hierophant with its rules, and The Star is what comes out into the world. The first triple occurs on 116 dates, the second on 169 — and all 169 of them fall on the 17th of the month.

In her book, Lisovskaya examines the line of a client: parents' point 9, children's point 12, outer expression 3. In our notation that is 3-12-9. The Hermit at home is a complete family in which everyone lives on their own wavelength and the child is left to themselves early. The Hanged Man in the attitude to children is service: the child becomes the centre of the world, the person gives them the attention they themselves went without and slides to the negative side, where care turns into control and reproaches. The Empress on the outside is a focus on the family and nothing else. The way out, for the author, is to restore contact with yourself and to help from a place of fullness rather than at your own expense. This line occurs on 324 dates, all of them on the 3rd or the 30th.

The section in the full reading is written on the same principle: each of the 255 triples gets its own title, a caption for each of the three cards and three paragraphs. They cover the childhood atmosphere and the mark it left, how it looks in life, and the difficulty, with a question to ask yourself and one manageable step. Two of these texts are given in full below.

article_sections.h2: A worked date, 12.04.2016: The Hanged Man, Strength and The Star
paragraphs: The 12-11-17 line turns up on 169 dates, 0.36% of them, roughly one in 274. Every one of them falls on the 12th: no other day gives a portrait of 12. And all of these dates share the same centre — 5.

**Why this conclusion.** The Star has long been called the card of hope — Waite records this reading, though he considers it the simplest one. Lisovskaya lists detachment from earthly matters and dependence on other people's opinions among the negative sides of this energy. She describes Strength as endurance and leadership which, on their negative side, turn into wearing yourself out and pressuring others. Her Hanged Man stands for compassion and service; her advice to it is to look at familiar things from a different angle, and on its negative side it means a state of suspension, self-sacrifice and an inability to say no. In this line the three ideas meet: support for others grows out of faith in better things, and your own postponed life pays for it.

article_sections.h2: The Fool in the attitude to children: The Hierophant, The Fool and The Star
paragraphs: The 5-22-17 line from the second worked date, 05.09.1990, turns up on 116 dates, 0.25% of them, roughly one in 399. All of these dates fall on the 5th or the 23rd, for people born between 1906 and 1993. The rule of twenty-two is easy to see here: 5 + 17 gives exactly 22, and The Fool stays The Fool.

**Why this conclusion.** For Lisovskaya, The Star stands for individuality, unusual taste and revealing your own uniqueness. The Fool is lightness, faith in miracles and freedom, and on its negative side, irresponsibility and — surprisingly — control over loved ones. She describes The Hierophant as passing on knowledge and family rules, and on its negative side as conservatism and pedantry; her advice to it is to teach without lecturing. Hence the idea of the triple: the freedom carried out of childhood looks for support in rules, and the question is where the two roles can meet.

article_sections.h2: How many parent-child lines there are and how common yours is

paragraphs: What makes a line common? It is set by just two numbers — the portrait A, which is the day of birth, and the centre E. That is why all the most common lines have a number from 5 to 10 at the outer point: each of these numbers gets two days a month. **The rarest triples are 8-11-3, 7-16-9, 6-12-6, 5-8-21 and 4-22-18:** each came up only twice, and all ten dates fall in January 2000.
The full check turned up a few more patterns:

ul: **Two identical numbers side by side only occur next to The Moon.** A and O match only when J is 18: from 5-5-18 to 11-11-18. O and J match only when A is 18: from 18-5-5 to 18-11-11. The two ends match in just two triples, 5-10-5 and 6-12-6. Three identical numbers never occur.

**Reversing the order gives a different line.** In 68 pairs both orders are possible, as with 5-22-17 and 17-22-5. The texts for such pairs are written separately: the childhood home and the outer expression are different roles.

**The line can repeat a neighbouring one.** For 5.5% of dates, A–O–J matches the talent line B–P–K — this happens exactly when the day arcanum equals the month. For 4.5% it matches material karma, and for 4.7% the karmic tail read from the corner to the centre. For example, 06.05.1995 has 6-19-13 as both its parent-child line and its material karma. Lisovskaya advises noticing such repeats, but the calculation cannot prove what they mean: that is her reading practice.

article_sections.h2: How an adult reads the line, and how a parent reads it for a child
paragraphs: **An adult reading for themselves.** The line describes you even if you have no children and don't plan to. O then means how you behave with everyone younger who depends on you: nephews and nieces, pupils, trainees, friends' children. It also covers how you react to someone else's noisy child on a train, and the private rule you once made for yourself. And J is not a verdict on your parents but the atmosphere you absorbed. It is easiest to recognise in small things: what was normal at home, what nobody talked about, what earned praise.

**A parent reading for a child.** If you calculate the line from your son's or daughter's date, J does not say what kind of parents you are; it says through which energy the child perceives home. Take it as a prompt to notice what matters to them in the family atmosphere, not as a verdict on your parenting. In a child, O is how they treat those younger and weaker than themselves: toddlers, pets, the toys in their games. It says nothing about their future children. How to read a child's whole chart is covered in a separate article on the child destiny matrix.

**Test it on yourself.** Write down the three keys of your triple and recall one episode for each: a moment from childhood you still remember; the last time you spent more than an hour with a child; what people who have only known you a short while usually say about you. If the episodes don't resemble the keys, don't force them to fit: perhaps another line is louder right now.

article_sections.h2: What the parent-child line does not show

ul: **How many children you will have, or when.** Neither the number of children, nor their sex, nor the timing of births follows from this line. If a calculator promises such a forecast, it is calculating something else.
**What actually happened in your family.** Three numbers are a symbolic reading of a theme, not a biography. What events took place at home cannot be derived from a date.
**Who is to blame.** The line neither accuses nor excuses your parents. It describes an atmosphere and the mark it left on you.
**Mother and father by number.** Lisovskaya uses a rule of thumb: "three is about the mother, four is about the father". This is her practice, not a law about any particular family.
**The purpose of an incarnation.** Lisovskaya links this line to the phrase "what we came to teach our parents", but that is her belief: a calculation from a date cannot prove it.

article_sections.h2: Free calculation and full reading: what you see where
paragraphs: For free you get the diagram with the label "Attitude to children" at point O, and the "Parent-child line" section with your three cards and the names of their roles. This article explains what each arcanum means in each role.
The full reading adds a connected text about your triple, built like the two examples above:

ul: its own title with the central idea of the combination;
a short caption for each card about what it does in its role;
three paragraphs: the childhood atmosphere and the mark it left, how it looks in life, and the difficulty, with a question to ask yourself and one step.

paragraphs: Such a text exists for every one of the 255 triples. Next in the report comes "Karma of relationships with parents and children" — the family rules of your lineage, read through points F, G and H.

ul: **Calculation** — by the formulas of the classic matrix: bottom corner D = A + B + C, centre E = A + B + C + D, J = A + E, O = A + J. Sums above 22 are reduced by adding their digits; 22 stays. Every number in this article comes from running all 46,334 dates from 1 January 1900 to 9 November 2026 through the calculator's engine: 255 triples, frequencies, impossible numbers, repeats and matches with neighbouring lines.

**The roles of the points and how to read the line** — Yuliana Lisovskaya, Matritsa Sudby dlya nachinayushchikh (The Destiny Matrix for Beginners): the chapter on points (the parents' point, the children's point, the point of outer expression), the chapter on lines, and the section "Parent-child karma (DRK)" in the chapter on integrating lines. The 9-12-3 example comes from the same book. The author uses her own numbers and letters for the points; the match with our A, O and J is based on their position on her diagram.

**The meanings of the arcana** — Lisovskaya's descriptions of the energies and the card imagery as Waite describes it. Waite did not create the destiny matrix method; applying the imagery to the roles of the line, and writing the readings, is our own work.

paragraphs: The automatic reading does an honest job of what it sets out to do: each part of the matrix is read separately. The parent-child line has its own text; talents, relationships and the family sections have theirs. In life, though, they don't live apart: your childhood home echoes in how you choose a partner, how you earn, what you allow yourself and children. The best way to start connecting the parts is to see them all on your own chart and follow each one to its page in the encyclopedia.

ul: **If the question is about you** — your childhood, your relationship with your parents, or why you behave the way you do around children — calculate your own matrix for free and find your A–O–J triple on the left-hand spoke. You don't need children for this.
**If the question is about you and your child**, enter both dates in the free compatibility calculator: it builds the matrix of two people, which describes the relationship rather than either of you.
**If you want to understand the child**, calculate the matrix from your child's date and read it alongside the article on the child destiny matrix.

paragraphs: The pages on each arcanum, the centre, the talent line and the "Parents and children" section are in the encyclopedia, so you can read every part of your chart in more depth.

faq.q: Which point on the diagram shows parent-child karma?
faq.a: On the left-hand spoke, running from the birth-day corner A to the centre. The spoke has three points — A at the edge, O in the middle, J next to the centre. On our diagram they are labelled "Personality portrait", "Attitude to children" and "Inner left point", and in the report the line has its own section, "Parent-child line". The same numbers appear in the physics column of the chakra table: A at Sahasrara, O at Ajna, J at Vishuddha.

faq.q: How do you calculate parent-child karma from a date of birth?
faq.a: First find the centre: D = day + month + year, E = day + month + year + D, where the year is the sum of its digits. Then J = day + E and O = day + J. Reduce every sum above 22 by adding its digits, and leave 22 as it is. Example — 12.04.2016: E = 5, J = 17, O = 29 → 11, so the line is 12-11-17.

faq.q: Do I need my parents' or my child's date of birth?
faq.a: No. The parent-child line is part of your personal matrix and is calculated from your date alone. Two dates are needed for a different question — the relationship between two specific people: for that you build a compatibility matrix.

faq.q: I don't have children. Is this line about me?
faq.a: Yes. O is your attitude to children in general and to the role of the elder: nephews and nieces, pupils, younger colleagues, someone else's child nearby. J is the atmosphere of your childhood, and A is how family experience comes out in you. None of the points says whether you will have children.

faq.q: Why do other sites say A is the parents and J the grandchildren?
faq.a: That is a different school. Many sites label the same three points like this: A — relationships with parents, O — with children, J — with grandchildren. Our site follows Lisovskaya: J is the parents' point, O the children's point, A the outer expression. The numbers in these schools can be the same, but the meaning of each point and the reading order differ.

faq.q: Another site gave me a different triple. Which one is wrong?
faq.a: Usually neither: calculators follow different rules. Some reduce sums above 22 by subtracting 22 instead of adding the digits: then the line comes out differently for almost every date — for 05.09.1990 it gives 5-10-5 instead of 5-22-17. Others write the triple in reverse, J–O–A. Others still leave out the middle point, and you have to work it out: O always equals the reduced sum of A and J.

faq.q: How is the parent-child line different from the "Parents and children" section?
faq.a: They use different points. The "Karma of relationships with parents and children" section reads the corners of the family square F, G and H: the rules of the male and female branches of the family and how you pass them on. The parent-child line reads A, O and J: the home you absorbed personally and your attitude to children. They share no points.

faq.q: Is a parent-child destiny matrix the same as parent–child compatibility?
faq.a: The phrase is sometimes used for both. Compatibility is built from two dates and describes the relationship between two specific people. The parent-child line is calculated from one date and describes one person. If your question is "how do I get on with my child?", you need the two-date matrix.

faq.q: Does the line show how many children I will have or when a child will be born?
faq.a: No. Neither the number of children, nor their sex, nor the timing of births follows from these three points. O describes your attitude to children: wishes, fears, how you behave around younger people.

faq.q: Does my triple mean that this is how things were in my family?
faq.a: No. It is a symbolic description of an atmosphere and the mark it left, not a biography. Test it against your own memories: if a key doesn't resemble your home, don't bend your memory to fit the key.

faq.q: Can parent-child karma be worked through or closed?
faq.a: Your triple stays with you for life, because your date of birth doesn't change. What changes is how you live out the line's energies — for example, noticing where you repeat a family pattern and choosing whether to keep it. No ritual will "close" the line, and the calculation offers none.

faq.q: Is the line different for men and women?
faq.a: No, the triple is the same: sex doesn't affect the calculation, so a man and a woman born on the same day share the same line.

faq.q: My Tarot deck numbers Strength 8. Why is it 11 here?
faq.a: This article, like the rest of the site, numbers the arcana in the Marseille tradition used in the destiny matrix: 11 is Strength, 8 is Justice, 22 is The Fool. In Waite's deck these two cards swap numbers. When you compare with a Tarot book, go by the card's name, not its number.
